::: {#exm-logistic-regression}

#### A six-patient trial

Six patients are split into a control group, coded $\predvar = -1$, and a treatment group, coded $\predvar = +1$.
The outcome is $\outvar = 1$ if the patient recovered.
Fitting the model of @eq-logistic-model by maximum likelihood gives the coefficients below.

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
# group coded -1 (control) and +1 (treatment); y = 1 means recovered
wf_x <- rep(c(-1, 1), each = 3)
wf_y <- c(0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1)
# maximum likelihood fit of the logistic model
wf_fit <- glm(wf_y ~ wf_x, family = binomial)
# the fitted intercept and slope
round(coef(wf_fit), 3)
```

The fitted slope is $\hcoef{1} = `r round(coef(wf_fit)[["wf_x"]], 3)`$.
The control group recovered at rate $1/3$ and the treatment group at $2/3$,
so the model fits both group proportions exactly.

:::
